sentences.text: JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 12-11-2022 at about 5-10 a.m., the petitioner was travelling in the Auto Rickshaw bearing No.KA-42-B-0859 along with others from Bidadi - Harohalli main road.

When the said Autorickshaw reached in front of Pathegowda Estate's Gate,
Kempayyanapalya village, Bidadi Hobli, Ramanagara Taluk & District, at that time Tata Sumo bearing Reg.No.KA-51-D-4350 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner came from Bidadi-Harohalli main road towards Kempayyanapalya village and dashed to the said Auto Rickshaw, result of which the said autorickshaw turned turtle thereby the petitioner and other passengers in the Auto Rickshaw sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Bharath Kempanna Hospital, Bidadi wherein admitted as an inpatient from 12-11-2022 to 14-11-2022.
So far the petitioner has spent Rs.1, 00,000/- towards treatment, medicine, conveyance and other incidental expenses.
The petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implant in future and she has to spent huge amount for her future treatment.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
The petitioner was dong coolie work besides her household works and earning more than Rs.18, 000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, petitioner is not in a position to do the said work and thereby petitioner and her entire family are put to great financial loss and mental agony.
4. On service of notice, the Respondent no.1 appeared through his counsel but has not filed written statement and thereby uncontested the petition.

5. Respondent no.2- /the insurer of Tata Sumo bearing No.KA-51-D-4350 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

It is further submitted that the accident in question has occurred due to the sole negligence of the driver of the auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-42-B-0859 as he was unmindful of the traffic and movements of vehicles on the road, without following lane discipline and giving way to the other vehicles dashed to the TATA Sumo vehicle.

The police without proper investigation deliberately registered accident case against the driver of insured TATA Sumo because Tata sumo is a bigger vehicle only to help the petitioner to have illegal and wrongful gains by way of compensation from the respondents.

2 6.

On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, she had sustained grievous injuries in the RTA alleged to have occurred on 12-11-2022 at about 05-10 a.m., near Papegowda Land,
Kempayyana Palya Village, Bidadi, Ramanagar Taluk & District, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tata Sumo bearing Reg.No.KA-51-D-4350?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as claimed? If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
7.
The petitioner got examined herself as Pw1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P9.

On the other hand, Saraswathi - the Manager is examined as RW.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.R1 to Ex.R3.
8.
Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and the respondent no.1 and perused the entire materials placed on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative. Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 : - In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 12-11-2022 at about 5-10 a.m. when the petitioner was travelling in the Auto Rickshaw bearing No.KA-42-B-0859 along with others from Bidadi - Harohalli main road and when the said Auto rickshaw reached in front of Pathegowda Estate's Gate,
Kempayyanapalya village, Bidadi Hobli, Ramanagara Taluk & District, at that time Tata Sumo bearing Reg.No.KA-51-D-4350 ( hereinafter referred to as offending the vehicle) driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner came from Bidadi-Harohalli main road towards Kempayyanapalya village and dashed to the said Auto Rickshaw, result of which said auto rickshaw turned turtle on the road and thereby petitioner and other passengers of the Auto Rickshaw sustained grievous injuries.

The P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 6 which are the police records such as F.I.R with Complaint, spot Jayamma vs Mukya Prana Travels on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23368797/
3 mahazar, notice u/Sec. 133 of IMV Act and reply given thereon, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet which are the material documents to prove the present issue.
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by petitioner/Jayamma, case has been registered against the driver of the offending vehicle in Crime No.0426/2022 of Bidadi Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of IPC.

After the completion of investigation, charge sheet was filed against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section under section 279, 337, 338 of IPC.
13.

If the spot mahazar is perused, Auto Rickshaw was proceeding on the left edge of Bidadi - Harohalli main road and the offending vehicle which came from opposite direction by driving the vehicle on the extreme right side of the road hit against the Auto Rickshaw in which the petitioner was travelling.

When the width of the said road is nearly 12 feet and the accident in question has occurred at a distance of 2 feet from the left edge of the tar road, it can be said that the driver of the offending vehicle by encroaching nearly 10 feet road by taking his vehicle on the extreme right side of his road has dashed against the Auto Rickshaw.
Hence, it can be said that the driver of the offending vehicle has contributed negligence.
The driver of the Auto Rickshaw was proceeding on the correct side of the road.
Hence, the driver of Auto Rickshaw has not contributed any amount of negligence.
Hence, issue no.1 is answered in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of her sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and Discharge summary which are marked at Ex.P.5 and Ex.P.8

On going through the medical documents, it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient at Bharath Kempanna Health Care, Bidadi,
Ramanagara from 12-11-2022 to 14-11- 2022 for a period of 2 days.
As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained one injury which is grievous in nature.
15. The petitioner has not examined the medical officer who has given treatment to her and no evidence on record to say that she has suffered permanent disability.
16. It is submitted by the petitioner that she was doing collie work and earning Rs.18, 000/- per month.

During the cross examination of PW.1, the learned counsel for respondent no 2 has confronted the xerox copy of pay slip but Pw1 has denied the said document and denied the fact of her working in Stove Kraft Limited.
It is the definite case of the respondent no.2 that petitioner was working in Stove Kraft Limited and earning Rs.12,000/- per month and after the accident also she has continued the job.
But as observed supra, the petitioner denied the fact of her working in Stove Craft Limited and submitted that she is working as coolie labour in the garden of one Sheenappa.
In order to substantiate the contention of the respondent no.2, they have summoned the Manager of Stove Craft Limited and examined her as Rw.1.

The RW.1 has deposed that since 2020 the petitioner is working as helper in Stove Craft Limited and drawing salary of Rs.12,244/- and that in the month of November -2023 the petitioner had availed leave without pay for 13 days and now also she is working in the very same company and that the petitioner possessed ESI card and the said ESI card is marked Ex.R1.
It is further deposed by RW.1 that for the 13 days of leave availed by the petitioner she was not paid with the salary.

sentences.text: From the evidence of respondent no.2 it can be gathered that the petitioner was working as helper in Stove Craft Limited and drawing salary of Rs.12,244/-.

Hence, the monthly income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.12,224/-.
18.

The respondent no.2 has contended that the petitioner is covered under the Employee's State Insurance Act and code number ESI No.5347032001 and Employee Code No.
53000402900000999 is allotted to her and that in view of the provision of Sec. 53 and 61 of Employees State Insurance Act, the claimant is covered under the provisions of ESI Act, hence petition is not maintainable and petitioner has to recourse to the remedy under ESI Act.

19. The learned counsel for respondent no.2 at this juncture has referred the judgment in MFA No.3796/2017 decided on 21-08-2023 between Smt. Puttamma Vs. The Managing Director, M/s VRL Logistics & Anr.
20.

entities.text: Smt. Puttamma Vs. The Managing Director, M/s VRL Logistics & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the judgment relied by the learned counsel for respondent no.2, referring Sec.53 and 61 of the Employees State Insurance Act it was held that "the petition under the Workmen's Compensation Act or the Employees Compensation Act is barred and the victim has to approach the ESI Corporation for compensation.
In the said case, the victim had applied for ESI facilities and code was allotted to the victim.
The subscription to the ESI facility was categorically stated by respondent no.1 and 2 in their written statement.
The said fact was not denied by the petitioner.
However they contended that they have not availed the compensation under the ESI Act.
In the above referred case, the Hon'ble High Court has made reference of several judgment rendered by Hon'ble High Court and Supreme Court.
In all the cases specific observation was made with reference to the word "Employment Injury suffered by the victim .
It means Sec. 53 and 61 of ESI Act would apply only to the Employment Injury suffered by the victim during the course of employment.
21. In the present case, the petitioner has not suffered injury during the course of Employment.
It is nowhere the case that petitioner has suffered injury during the course of employment.
The present petition is not filed under ECA.
Hence, the observation made in the aforesaid ruling has no application to the case in hand.
Hence, the claim petition filed by the petitioner is very well maintainable.
22. Towards pain and sufferings, the petitioner shown to have sustained one grievous injury.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment etc it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering.

23. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner, she has produced medical bills for Rs.37,550/-
as per Ex.P.9.
As such petitioner is entitled for Rs.37,550/- under the head medical expenses.

24. Further for 3 days of hospitalization at Bharath Kempanna Health Care and for her taking follow up treatment in the said hospital, requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment, for Jayamma vs Mukya Prana Travels on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23368797/
5 follow-ups has incurred traveling expenses, she has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.12,000/-.
25.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injury and taken treatment for 3 days as inpatient.
As per the evidence of Rw.1 the petitioner has taken leave without pay for 13 days and thereafter she has continued the job.
Hence, the period of 15 days is taken as laid down period.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.6,122/- towards loss of income during the laid down period.
26. The petitioner at her age of 50 years has suffered grievous injuries.
Hence taking in to consideration the said aspect the petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities and discomforts.

The Petitioner is entitled compensation under the following heads:
Sl. Heads Amount No.
1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs.50,000/-
2. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs.12,000/-
 charges and nourishing food 3.

Medical expenses Rs.37,550/-
4. Loss of income during laid down Rs. 6,122/-
 period Loss of discomfort and amenities Rs.50,000/-
Total Rs.1,55,672/-

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,55,672/- (Rupees One Lakh Fifty Five Thousand Six Hundred Seventy Two only).
27.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.2 this court directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
28. Issue No.3:
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.1,55,672/- + cost of Rs.500/- imposed vide order on IA -II.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.1,56,172/- (Rupees One Lakh Fifty Six Hundred One Hundred Seventy Two only).

6
A Sum of Rs.1,55,672/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.
On deposit entire amount and interest is ordered to be released in favour of the petitioner on proper identification Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 7 th day of November, 2024.)
